title: Potential farther from a charge
hook: Change distance and predict electric-potential magnitude.
misconception: electric-potential magnitude doubles when distance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r to compare electric-potential magnitude when distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed point charge with zero potential at infinity, potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r. When distance doubles, electric-potential magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed point charge with zero potential at infinity, with a nonzero initial result. If distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-potential magnitude?
recall.why: Apply potential magnitude = k·abs(q)/r under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
